topic_and_scope: This narrative review surveys global diabetic retinopathy (DR) burden, diagnostic advances, treatment modalities, and health-system strategies, highlighting disparities in care and the potential of AI, telemedicine, and innovative therapies to improve screening, treatment access, and outcomes. Notes: the field should prioritize long-term validation of emerging technologies, equitable implementation across resource settings, and integration of multidisciplinary care with patient education and policy support.
main_themes: AI-enabled screening, telemedicine, and advanced imaging to enable scalable, equitable early detection of DR across diverse health systems
Current and evolving therapeutic landscape for DR, including anti-VEGF therapy (and faricimab) with extended dosing intervals, biosimilars, and combined laser/surgical approaches

Future directions in personalized medicine and innovative therapies (RIP1 inhibitors, gene therapy, stem cell therapy, SGLT2 inhibitors, fenofibrate, Ang-2 inhibitors) within multidisciplinary care models and implementation challenges
main_findings: AI-assisted image analysis and telemedicine platforms can enhance early detection of DR and expand access to screening in resource-limited settings, though adoption faces data privacy, regulatory, and equity challenges

Anti-VEGF therapy remains the cornerstone of DR treatment with advances such as faricimab showing longer injection intervals and potential superior outcomes; biosimilars may improve affordability and access, while targeted combinations with laser or surgical interventions may optimize long-term vision outcomes

key_gaps.description: Need for long-term, large-scale real-world validation of emerging technologies (AI, telemedicine, imaging modalities) and new therapeutics to establish safety, efficacy, and generalizability across diverse populations
Persistent inequities in access to advanced DR therapies and technologies in resource-limited settings, requiring policy, financing, and scalable delivery models to ensure health equity

future_directions.title: Scale and validate explainable AI–enabled teleophthalmology for DR screening across diverse health systems
future_directions.rationale: Given the demonstrated potential of AI and telemedicine to improve DR detection in underserved areas, prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate performance, ensure explainability, address regulatory and privacy concerns, and integrate workflows with primary care and ophthalmology MDTs. Steps include developing standardized imaging protocols, creating interoperable data pipelines, conducting implementation science evaluations, and establishing regulatory frameworks for AI decision-support in DR screening.

future_directions.title: Conduct prospective real-world trials comparing faricimab with conventional anti-VEGF regimens across diverse populations
future_directions.rationale: Faricimab has shown extended treatment intervals and edema reduction in key trials, suggesting reduced burden and improved adherence. Real-world data across regions with varying access and comorbidity profiles are needed to confirm safety, efficacy, and optimal dosing schedules, and to identify subgroups that benefit most from dual VEGF-A/Ang-2 inhibition.

future_directions.title: Pilot cost-effective anti-VEGF delivery models and devices suitable for low-resource settings
future_directions.rationale: Access barriers limit DR treatment in many regions. Initiatives should evaluate biosimilars, low-cost intravitreal delivery systems, and streamlined clinic workflows, including community-based injection programs and portable imaging, to expand coverage while maintaining safety and efficacy.

future_directions.title: Advance early-phase trials of RIP1 inhibitors for neuroprotection in DR
future_directions.rationale: Preclinical data indicate necroptotic pathway inhibition may preserve retinal neurons. Phase I/II trials are needed to assess safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy in DR to determine viability as a neuroprotective strategy alongside vascular-targeted therapies.

future_directions.title: Accelerate translation of gene therapy and stem cell therapies for refractory DR
future_directions.rationale: Gene editing and stem cell approaches hold promise for restoring retinal structure and regulating angiogenesis, but require rigorous clinical trials to establish long-term safety, dosing, delivery methods, and functional outcomes. Priorities include standardized endpoints, robust adverse-event monitoring, and ethical/regulatory alignment.

future_directions.title: Evaluate SGLT2 inhibitors and fenofibrate for early DR in diverse populations
future_directions.rationale: Emerging data suggest vascular and metabolic benefits may slow DR progression, particularly in early disease. Well-designed RCTs and mechanistic studies should define patient populations, dosing, and combination strategies with standard anti-VEGF therapy and lifestyle interventions.

future_directions.title: Integrate biomarker- and genetics-informed personalization into MDT DR care
future_directions.rationale: Genetic and molecular biomarkers (e.g., VEGF polymorphisms) could guide choice and timing of anti-VEGF therapy, while systemic risk factor optimization (HbA1c, blood pressure, lipids) should be aligned with ocular treatment within multidisciplinary teams. Prospective studies should identify predictive markers, develop decision-support tools, and embed precision approaches into standard care pathways.
